name: חיבור שברים – מונים ומכנים לינאריים (באנגלית)
questiontext:
Express the following as a single fraction in its lowest terms:

\[ \frac{{CT:0}}{{CT:1}}+\frac{{CT:2}}{{CT:3}}. \]

[[input:ans]]
[[validation:ans]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: Take the product of the two denominators as the common denominator, add the fractions, open the brackets in the numerator, then cancel any common factor.
Step 1 — The common denominator
When adding fractions with linear expressions the method remains the same. Firstly, find a suitable common denominator and add the fractions. When you have linear expressions in the denominator it is usually best to take the common factor as the product of the denominators (i.e. \({{CT:4}}\)). In this example:

\[ \frac{{CT:0}}{{CT:1}}+\frac{{CT:2}}{{CT:3}} = \frac{{CT:5}}{{CT:4}}+\frac{{CT:6}}{{CT:4}} = \frac{{CT:7}}{{CT:4}} \]

Step 2 — Open the brackets in the numerator
After adding, collect the 'like terms':

\[ {{CT:7}}={{CT:8}}+{{CT:9}}={{CT:10}} \]

Step 3 — Lowest terms
Cancel any common factors from the numerator and the denominator. [[if test="{{CT:15}}"]]The numerator and the denominator still have a common factor. Factorise both and cancel it:

\[ \frac{{{CT:10}}}{{{CT:11}}}=\frac{{{CT:12}}}{{{CT:13}}} \]

[[else]]Factorise the numerator: it has no factor in common with the denominator, so nothing cancels and the fraction is in its lowest terms.[[/if]]

\[ \frac{{CT:0}}{{CT:1}}+\frac{{CT:2}}{{CT:3}} = \frac{{CT:5}}{{CT:4}}+\frac{{CT:6}}{{CT:4}} = \frac{{CT:7}}{{CT:4}} = {{CT:14}}. \]

on_true.feedback: You cannot add fractions by adding the numerator and the denominator. You must find a common denominator and then add the numerators, or use the general rule: \( \frac{a}{c}+\frac{b}{d} = \frac{ad+bc}{cd} \)

on_false.feedback: Your answer is equal to the sum, but the fraction is not in lowest terms: the numerator and the denominator have a common factor. Cancel it.
